To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation in patients with con- comitant heart failure is associated with lower heart failure hospitalizations and mortality compared to medical therapy.
catheter ablation of AF in patients with con- current AF and HF is associated with a significant reduction in HF hospitalizations and a trend toward a reduction in all-cause mortality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the analysis of the data from the analysis of the heart failure.
the development of a novel approach to the development of the AF ablation in heart failure — a novel approach to ablation.
the development of new methods and tools to study and treat atrial fibrillation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CASTLE-Af trial provides evidence for a beneficial effect of AF ablation on HF hospitalizations and mortality.

AF ablation should be considered in patients with AF and HF, especially if the patient is symptomatic from AF, and that this procedure is associated with significant reduction in HF hospitalization and mortality.
AF ablation should be considered in HF patients with symptomatic AF and/or recurrent AF, as it is associated with improved quality of life and reduced hospitalizations and mortality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AF is a major contributor to HF, and AF ablation should be considered for patients with HF and concomitant AF.
AF ablation is associated with a significant improvement in quality of life, and a significant reduction in HF hospitalization and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality.
ablation of AF in patients with HF is safe and effective and should be strongly considered in these patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current guidelines should be revised to include AF ablation as a Class I recommendation in patients with concur­rent AF and HF.
AF ablation in this population of patients is associated with a reduction in HF hospitalization and mortality.
AF ablation should be considered as a treatment option in this high-risk population.
